key_insight: A Fourier neural operator learns the evolution of nonlinear standing waves along a numerically computed one-parameter family, with small in-distribution relative errors.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a surrogate for repeated evaluations of idealized free-surface wave dynamics across observation times and wave profiles.
method: Train on a one-parameter family of symmetric standing waves in two-dimensional, infinitely deep, inviscid flow.
Map a surface profile at rest and normalized observation time to the surface, velocity potential, and surface dipole density.
Assess predictions using reference solutions and an independently evaluated governing-equation residual.
evidence_signal: Tests show uniformly small in-distribution relative errors; extrapolation produces crest-localized errors near the free-fall limit and rising relative errors as amplitudes approach zero.
watch_item: Generalization beyond the sampled wave family is unestablished, and spectral truncation limits accuracy near sharpening crests.
paper_title: Learning the solution operator of standing waves with a Fourier neural operator
